newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Argentine central banker sees 96 GDP near 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Argentine central banker sees 96 GDP near 3 pct.

text.p: Former Argentine central bank president Javier Gonzalez Fraga, said he expects an annualized growth rate of just below 3.0 percent in Argentina in 1996, with exports leading the way.
Gonzalez Fraga, speaking to a meeting sponsored by the Americas Society here, said: "My forecast for the year is slightly below 3.0 percent GDP (gross domestic product)."
Currently chairman of the Argentine Institute of Capital Markets, Gonzalez Fraga said, "This growth of 3.0 percent is being led by investments of exports. It is no longer a consumption-led boom."
In 1997, Gonzalez Fraga expects growth to be about 3.5 percent.

He also said he expects inflation to run around 1.0 percent in October. "We had almost no inflation in the last four months...but we expect 1.0 pct inflation in October, and that would bring inflation for the whole year to about 1.1 percent."
In terms of 1997 borrowings, Gonzalez Fraga said he expects Argentina to raise about $10 billion as long as favorable market conditions continue.
On the banking front, Gonzalez Fraga said positive developments recently include the completion of most of the privatizations of Argentina's provincial banks.
Other major developments in Argentina include an agreement reached with the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) on instituting a futures and options market, he said.
While Gonzalez Fraga believes political turbulence over the next three years will mount, he still remains optimistic about Argentina over the longer-term.

"I understand that the coming three years will be difficult, but...it will improve and I remain an optimist about the long term," said Gonzalez Fraga, noting that "the challenge for Argentina is to consolidate the economy regardless of the risks."
